headline: Kyle Drops a Nuke, Olave Garden Wins by Accident, and the Bo Nix Swap Heard 'Round Delt Dynasty
subhead: Week 11 featured a 215-point clinic, a 60-point bench fart, and a trade so cosmically dumb it altered the standings.
matchOfTheWeek: Put an AR to My Head dropped 215.06 on 226 Alpha and it wasn't even a game — it was a war crime with 95.3% lineup efficiency. Amon-Ra (38.7), Goff (34.58), and Saquon (33.8) all went nuclear while Szara watched Matthew Stafford rot on his bench for 27.8 points. The 71.22-point margin is the kind of result that should come with grief counseling and a FEMA application.
mainRecap:
Let's start with Kyle, because nothing else in Week 11 matters quite as much as a man putting up 215 points and his entire Lions stack going supernova on the same Sunday. Amon-Ra cooked, Goff carved, Saquon stomped, and 226 Alpha got reduced to a stain. Szara, you scored 143.84 — a perfectly respectable number — and lost by 71. There is no scheme, no waiver, no prayer that fixes this. Stafford going for 27.8 on your bench is just God laughing at you.

Then there's The Olave Garden, who won 161.72 to 139.72 and STILL left 60.92 points on the bench, headlined by Taysom Hill posting a 46.52 from the pine. Patrick, you scored 222.64 in your sleep and benched it — that's not a lineup, that's a fumble in cleats. Even better: you literally just traded FOR Bo Nix and he hung 28.78 on his former owner. Speaking of which — Bo Nix Celli, you traded away the guy in your team name, got Brock Bowers' 37.8-point monster game, and still lost. Chris Olave better be worth it because right now it looks like you swapped a Ferrari for a scratch-off.

Elsewhere, Hot Cocks survived MassiveCocks in a battle for the most legally questionable team names, with Mixon's 35.3 just barely outrunning Tee Higgins' 29.8. LargestofRocks rolled the Good Ladds behind Breece Hall (31.1), while Mig wonders why he started anyone not named Noah Gray (20.3 on the bench, woof). Stroud Boys posted the league's lowest score (108.54) and somehow Jonnu Smith outscored half their starters with 31.1 — Jewett, your team is literally one tight end and a prayer. T swift's Baddies left Jameis Winston's 26.6 on the bench because of course they did, and Jets' Juniors celebrated their playoff push by trading for… Derek Carr. Mattwunder, buddy. This is a SuperFlex league, not a hostage negotiation.

powerRankings.blurb: Hung 215 with 95% efficiency — Kyle isn't running a fantasy team, he's running a lab experiment on human suffering.

Mixon's 35.3 carried you past your dong-named rival; enjoy the W before someone notices the roster.
Breece Hall ate, you won by 26, and you still found a way to bench 21 points of Zach Ertz — peak Rocks behavior.
38-point win over the Baddies looks great until you remember you traded actual assets for Derek Carr.
37.8 from Bowers, a fresh Olave in the building, and still an L because you traded the guy in your team name — poetic.
Quietly dropped 132 and dispatched Stroud Boys; the most invisible 23-point win in league history.
Tee Higgins gave you 29.8 and you still lost the Battle of the Phallic Names — heartbreaking.
118 points and Noah Gray hung 20 in street clothes — Mig, this is a coaching issue.
Lost by 38 with Jameis cooking 26.6 on your bench; the Era ended approximately three weeks ago.
League-low 108 with Jonnu Smith doing 30% of the work — the rest of the roster is on a milk carton.
Lost by 71 with Stafford's 27.8 on the bench; the only Alpha in this name is the one in 'Alpha Centauri,' which is where this season needs to be launched.
